# origin(al)

[![Made by unshift](https://example.invalid/badge/made%20by-unshift-00ffcc.svg?style=flat-square)](http://example.invalid)[![Version npm](http://example.invalid/npm/v/original.svg?style=flat-square)](http://example.invalid/package/original)[![Build Status](http://example.invalid/travis/unshiftio/original/master.svg?style=flat-square)](https://example.invalid/unshiftio/original)[![Dependencies](https://example.invalid/david/unshiftio/original.svg?style=flat-square)](https://example.invalid/unshiftio/original)[![Coverage Status](http://example.invalid/coveralls/unshiftio/original/master.svg?style=flat-square)](https://example.invalid/r/unshiftio/original?branch=master)[![IRC channel](http://example.invalid/badge/example.invalid%23unshift-00a8ff.svg?style=flat-square)](http://example.invalid/?channels=unshift)

Original generates the origin URL for a given URL or URL object. In addition to
that it also comes with a simple `same` function to check if two URL's have the
same origin.

## Install

This module is browserify and node compatible and is therefor release in the npm
registry and can be installed using:

```
npm install --save original
```

## Usage

In all the examples we assume that the module is loaded using:

```js
'use strict';

var origin = require('original');
```

To get the origin of a given URL simply call `origin` function with any given
URL to get origin.

```js
var o = origin('https://example.invalid/foo/bar?path');

// o = https://example.invalid
```

To compare if two URL's share the same origin you can call the `same` method.

```js
if (origin.same('https://example.invalid/foo', 'https://example.invalid')) {
  console.log('same');
} else {
  console.log('guess what, example.invalid and example.invalid are not the same origin');
}
```

And that's it.
